title: Training waits on the DataLoader (num_workers=0)
score_basis: measured data-wait share of step time
evidence: 34% of step time is spent waiting for the next batch (13.7 ms per step) and the DataLoader runs with num_workers=0, so loading and the training step take turns on one core.
suggestion: Set num_workers=5 and persistent_workers=True on the DataLoader. On macOS and Windows workers start with spawn: keep the training code under `if __name__ == "__main__":` and make sure the dataset pickles.
expected_effect: At most 1.52x (the step time without any data wait), reached only if loading fully overlaps compute.
risk_note: Deterministic datasets give identical batches. Random augmentation in workers draws from per-worker RNG streams, so exact samples differ (same distribution). Each worker holds a copy of the dataset in memory.

title: Per-sample preprocessing in RawRows is expensive
score_basis: data-wait share times the __getitem__ share of it, times 0.9 so the one-line worker fix ranks first when both apply
evidence: 34% of step time is data wait and 69% of that is inside RawRows.__getitem__ (0.04 ms per sample).
suggestion: Make preprocessing cheaper instead of (or as well as) parallelizing it: precompute or cache deterministic transforms once, move per-element Python loops to vectorized tensor ops on the whole batch (or on the device), and keep only cheap random augmentation per sample.
expected_effect: At most 1.52x if data wait disappears entirely.
risk_note: Only safe if the cached or vectorized path produces the same tensors. compare's loss check catches a transform that changed.

title: No mixed precision on hardware that supports it
score_basis: 0.1 x compute ('other') share of step time
evidence: Device mps, this torch build supports autocast on MPS; autocast was never entered and parameters are float32. 63% of step time is compute and Python ('other').
suggestion: Wrap the forward pass and loss in `with torch.autocast('mps', dtype=torch.float16):`. Gains on Apple GPUs vary by op, so measure.
expected_effect: Largest on compute-bound models dominated by matmuls and convolutions; little or none when data loading or sync dominates.
risk_note: Lower precision changes numerics. bf16 rarely needs loss scaling; fp16 needs GradScaler. Check the loss trajectory with compare.

title: torch.compile is not used
score_basis: prior 0.03 for mps x compute ('other') share
evidence: torch 2.14.1 supports torch.compile and it was never called. 63% of step time is compute and Python overhead, which is what compilation reduces.
suggestion: Try `model = torch.compile(model)`. Support for MPS is newer than for CUDA and CPU; expect some models to fall back or run slower. Compare with more warmup steps (for example --warmup-steps 20): compilation happens in the first steps.
expected_effect: Fewer kernel launches and less Python overhead per step. Compilation adds startup time, so it pays off on long runs.
risk_note: Same math in principle, but fused kernels can differ in the last bits, and graph breaks or recompiles can make a run slower. Measure.
